exp: Both metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity are risk factors for chronic kidney disease, so normal metabolic markers are not reassuring.

evidence.quote: Conclusion Overweight and obesity are associated with an increased incidence of CKD in metabolically healthy young and middle-aged participants. These findings show that metabolically healthy obesity is not a harmless condition and that the obese phenotype, regardless of metabolic abnormalities, can adversely affect renal function.

q: What is the lowest point of the BMI curve, occurring at about six years of age, called?
src: Rolland-Cachera, M. F., Deheeger, M., Bellisle, F., Sempé, M., Guilloud-Bataille, M., & Patois, E. (1984). Adiposity rebound in children: A simple indicator for predicting obesity. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 39(1), 129–135. https://doi.org/10.1093/ajcn/39.1.129
exp: The BMI curve rises in infancy, reaches its lowest point at around six years and then rises again; that nadir is the adiposity rebound.

evidence.quote: Adiposity increases during the 1st yr and then decreases. A renewed rise, termed here the adiposity rebound, occurs at about 6 yr.

q: What is the prognosis for a child with an early adiposity rebound?
a: They tend to end growth with a higher level of adiposity
They naturally return to average BMI in adolescence
There is no relation to adult obesity risk
Only the risk of short stature increases
src: Rolland-Cachera, M. F., Deheeger, M., Bellisle, F., Sempé, M., Guilloud-Bataille, M., & Patois, E. (1984). Adiposity rebound in children: A simple indicator for predicting obesity. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 39(1), 129–135. https://doi.org/10.1093/ajcn/39.1.129
exp: Early adiposity rebound is an early indicator of adult obesity, whereas children with a late rebound tend to return to average BMI in late adolescence.

evidence.quote: The present study shows a relationship between the age at adiposity rebound and final adiposity. An early rebound (before 5.5 yr) is followed by a significantly higher adiposity level than a later rebound (after 7 yr). This phenomenon is observed whatever the subject's adiposity at 1 yr.
evidence.note: The cohort ran from 1 month to 16 years, so "final adiposity" means adiposity at the end of growth, not measured adult weight status; the adulthood persistence in the answer goes beyond this paper.

Pediatric obesity—Assessment, treatment, and prevention: An Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, 102(3), 709–757. https://doi.org/10.1210/jc.2016-2573
exp: Rising weight with slowing height growth suggests an endocrine cause such as hypothyroidism or growth hormone deficiency and calls for immediate investigation.

evidence.quote: Pediatric obesity has its basis in genetic susceptibilities influenced by a permissive environment starting in utero and extending through childhood and adolescence. Endocrine etiologies for obesity are rare and usually are accompanied by attenuated growth patterns.
evidence.note: The abstract links endocrine causes of obesity to attenuated (slowed) linear growth, which is the rationale behind the answer, but it does not say that this combination is an indication for urgent investigation. The explicit recommendation is in the guideline body (recommendation on evaluating children with obesity and short stature/decreased growth velocity).

q: What proportion of children with obesity have an underlying endocrine or genetic cause for their weight gain?
a: Rare - most cases are primary (simple) obesity

exp: Most have primary or simple obesity with normal or rapid growth; endocrine work-up is warranted mainly when linear growth slows.

q: In the WHO recommendations, what is the minimum daily moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for children and adolescents aged five to 18?
src: Bull, F. C., Al-Ansari, S. S., Biddle, S., Borodulin, K., Buman, M. P., Cardon, G., Carty, C., Chaput, J.-P., Chastin, S., Chou, R., Dempsey, P. World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 54(24), 1451–1462. https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955
exp: At least 60 minutes a day, plus vigorous muscle- and bone-strengthening activities at least three times per week; moderate intensity is the point where speaking becomes difficult.

evidence.quote: Recommendations for children and adolescents (5–17 years) The evidence affirmed that physical activity in children and adolescents is associated with improved physical, mental and cognitive health outcomes. Many of the benefits of physical activity are observed with an average of 60 min of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) daily, although physical activity beyond 60 min of MVPA daily provide additional health benefits.
